steps.content: And so, Parfait brings along her whole crew of West District friends—plus you, dragged along against your better judgment—to attend the annual Spring Concert.

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: Ugh, this stupid suit collar's choking me. Rich people's clothes really are all just for show...
Cyllis wears a beautiful cocktail dress, though she seems equally uneasy, her voice dropping to a hushed tone as she speaks.

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: You think you're the only one feeling uncomfortable? Please, the rest of us are sucking it up too. Eastsiders got eyes everywhere.

Old Rayden, by contrast, remains relatively composed. After all, he is from an older generation of the West District residents, one that has lived through the district's golden age. He's seen his fair share of the world.
Still, the hostile glares from the surrounding Eastsiders unsettle even him, and he keeps fiddling with his tie without realizing it.

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: Tch, it's not just these guys down here. Even those rich pricks up in the fancy seats are getting their kicks watching us squirm. Seriously, what's the damn point of us even being here?

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: We're already here.
Old Rayden gives you a worried glance, concerned that being seen with them might embarrass you too. After all, it took considerable persuasion on your part to get them all to come tonight...

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: No freakin' way! Parfait's gone completely off the rails still hung up on that damn concert. Seriously?! You gotta be kidding me!

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: That's right, Chief. I know Parfait's all about those fancy arts and performances. If she wants to go by herself, that's her business. But hauling a bunch of us along when we don't even have proper clothes to wear...

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: Besides, she's already walking on thin ice. If we show up, her cover's toast for sure. After that? No way she could ever go back to Eastside, even if she wanted to.
Hold on... Let's address these concerns one at a time.
First, Parfait has already arranged formal outfits for you guys to wear to the performance.

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: Such a waste of money... And it's not like she's flush with cash these days, is she?
Well... custom formal wear can't be returned. Even if you don't go, Parfait wouldn't get any money back.

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: What? That's...
About Parfait's identity situation, don't worry about that anymore. Truth is, even Parfait has stopped caring about it at this point.
Right now, she's completely surrounded by enemies over in Eastside. They're literally everywhere, and she genuinely needs your protection.

I've done all the convincing you asked me to do, and Parfait didn't raise any objections. Once we're done with this performance, if Eastside really becomes too dangerous for her, she'll probably come back here.

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: I guess... that's fine.

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: Hell no! You wanna go make fools of yourselves? Be my guest! But I'm not walking into Eastside just to get looked down on!
This is the one thing you truly can't control. You can handle all the other practical problems, but there's no way to influence how the Eastsiders will see them.
So you grit your teeth...
...And agree to attend the concert with them, to "lend them some backing."

Almost immediately, you regret it. You really don't want to go. No matter how the others feel, you know your own experience will be miserable. At the very least, those speculators—the ones desperate to get a cut of the West District Hypercube mining operation—wouldn't miss the chance to corner you after the show.

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: Ugh, this stupid collar. I wanna just tear it right off! Look at Chief over there, all relaxed in regular clothes and a hat. Way better than being stuck in this stuffy getup.

You shrink back slightly, guilt creeping in. Before coming here, you debated for ages but ultimately decided to put together a disguise, hoping the Eastside merchants upstairs and downstairs wouldn't recognize you.
It goes against your promise to lend them some backing... but, well, better safe than sorry!

steps.speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
steps.content: Look, there's the investment guru with her Syndicate friends...
And karma has already caught up with you. The murmuring around you is becoming too loud to ignore.

steps.speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
steps.content: Hmph... They could wrap themselves in the finest silks and still reek of commonness. Some things simply can't be polished away.

steps.speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
steps.content: You'll never guess what the investment guru has done now. She actually sold the VIP ticket Miss Ava graciously gave her, just to drag along that ragtag entourage she calls friends.

steps.speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
steps.content: Oh, really? The New Year's address later is meant to be hers, isn't it? My my, how the mighty have tumbled.

steps.speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
steps.content: Haha, don't you know? When Mr. McLenn and those other investors who lost money found out Parfait was bringing Syndicans, they deliberately set this whole thing up.

steps.speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
steps.content: Shh, keep your voice down. The Syndicans might hear...

steps.speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
steps.content: So what? They could brave appearing in this place, but my words are suddenly too much for their fragile sensibilities?
You watch as Ed slams his hand against the armrest beside you. If Cyllis weren't holding him down, he'd be on his feet in an instant.

Meanwhile, Parfait, the one truly at the eye of the storm, sits at the front of your group, seemingly oblivious. Her attention remains fixed on the slowly rising curtain, her gaze never wavering for even a second.

steps.speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
steps.content: Look at that idiot. One little remark and he's already fuming.

steps.speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
steps.content: Careful now. They might beat you up.

steps.speaker: Neighboring Concertgoer
steps.content: Don't be absurd. This is Eastside, not some Syndicate gutter where their kind can do as they please...
Veins bulge visibly on Cyllis's forehead now, too. Without hesitation, she snaps off the heel of her shoe and rises to her feet beside Ed, her movements deliberate.
Then, the lighting shifts—and there, under the spotlight, stands a tall, elegant figure.

The thick tension in the air dissipates in an instant. Below the stage, Eastsiders and West District residents alike turn their eyes upward, drawn to the presence now commanding the space. A hush falls over the crowd as they wait for Parfait's first words, each person harboring their own private expectations.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Ladies and gentlemen, and to all the brilliant minds tuning in live or catching the rerun, whether you're here with us in person or cozied up at home: a very good morning, afternoon, and evening to you!
Under the spotlight and in front of the cameras, Parfait effortlessly slips back into her role as the legendary investment guru, radiating a remarkable sense of ease and confidence.
A smattering of halfhearted applause rises from the audience. The Eastsiders barely acknowledge her greeting, clapping only to exchange smirks and whispers, clearly waiting for her to stumble.
Unfazed by the lukewarm reception, Parfait keeps her smile steady, patiently waiting for the scattered applause to die down.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: My name is Parfait, though you likely know me as the "investment guru." A title I find terribly dramatic, but who am I to argue with results? Truthfully, I've just been lucky, always managing to pick the winning side in my investments.
Parfait breaks into a wide grin, her white teeth almost dazzling under the lights.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I imagine many of you are wondering... why, of all people, am I the one giving this New Year's address? Well, allow me to explain.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Ever since N.F. 108, when stand-up comedian Aaron first delivered that unforgettable speech at the Spring Concert, the organizers have made a tradition of inviting the year's most outstanding comedian to take the stage. And why not? This is the Spring Concert, a joyous occasion where we might as well start the year with laughter. But...

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Ah, I see those puzzled looks. You're probably thinking: Wait, isn't this woman supposed to be some "investment guru"? What's she got to do with comedy? Well, my dear audience, here's the punchline—

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Turns out, this so-called "investment guru" spent the second half of the year turning herself into the biggest joke of all.
The moment she says this, the audience erupts in laughter.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I invested in a promising venture in the Outlands, only to return to DisCity and find everything in shambles.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: My business partners? Vanished. The company? Buried under a mountain of bad debts. And if not for Mr. McLenn's generous help, I wouldn't even have scraped together enough for tickets for my friends and myself to attend tonight.
As Parfait speaks, she presses a hand to her heart and gestures toward the VIP seats—a silent "Thank you, McLenn, our friendship lives right here."
The camera cuts to McLenn at the perfect moment. Caught in the swell of cheers and applause, he cannot but nod and flash an awkward smile to the lens.
When the crowd finally settles, the camera swings back to Parfait. Smiling, she lifts the microphone and smoothly moves on.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: But seriously, what an unforgettable year, don't you think?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: So much has happened. The highs, the lows, moments that broke our hearts and others that lifted us right back up. How do you even sum up a year like this? "Epic"? "A rollercoaster"? "Shakespearean drama"?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: ...Forgive me, words fail me sometimes. Then again, as you all know, I am from the West District. We weren't exactly raised on the finest education.

The entire venue goes silent for a beat, then a wave of murmurs ripples through the crowd. The audience didn't expect Parfait to acknowledge the rumors about her past, let alone address them so openly. For a moment, no one seems sure how to react, until someone begins to clap, and the rest follow suit.
Amid the rising applause, Parfait smiles and continues.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Fortunately, we still have this Spring Concert, with these extraordinary musicians and the magnificent Maestro Euragio gracing us tonight.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: And that, my friends, is the magic of music and art. Whether you're an Eastsider, a West District resident, or even an Outlander—whether your pockets are heavy or light, your heart full or aching—music...

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: ...Music has a way of stealing your truest emotions right in the moment. Then, like a master alchemist, it weaves them together with everything we've lived through this year, transforming them into something exquisite. Unforgettable.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: So, without further ado, ladies and gentlemen, let the N.F. 115 Spring Concert begin!

With a dramatic sweep of her hand, the curtains part behind Parfait, revealing the stage. The atmosphere in the venue reaches fever pitch. After all, the "investment guru's" speeches never fail to captivate, bending even the most reluctant minds to her will.
When she promises the most wonderful music, no one doubts they're about to experience a truly sumptuous musical feast.
With a final smile, Parfait steps off the stage and slips into her seat beside you and the other West District residents.
Then, joyful, magnificent music swells through the air, and the long-awaited concert begins.

The performance continues, one piece seamlessly blending into the next. And in a way, you have to admit, Parfait is right. There's a world of difference between listening to music at home or on a screen and feeling the infectious energy of a live performance.
And that energy works its magic. Slowly, the thick, acrid tension in the air dissolves as the music washes over the crowd, pulling every gaze toward the stage.
When Maestro Euragio, the very musician Parfait has constantly mentioned, steps into the spotlight, you find yourself glancing her way.

Wonder. Satisfaction. Pure, unguarded enjoyment. The woman the Eastsiders whisper about as some "great fraud" is utterly spellbound, her eyes alight with a passion so fierce it's almost too much to take in.
As the maestro takes a deep bow on stage for his final curtain call, the Spring Concert comes to an end.
Parfait is right. This is the kind of performance you can't afford to miss. Anyone who's ever felt music move them—even just a little—will remember this night for years to come.
Amid thunderous applause that lingers long enough to blur your vision, you and the West District group slip out just ahead of the crowd, while the rest of the audience remains lost in the afterglow.

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: Doo doo... dee doo dee doo...
Ed starts humming a tune, and you recognize it. It's the last piece the maestro performed.

steps.speaker: Cyllis
steps.content: Not bad humming there, Ed. I didn't know you had that kind of talent.
Ed's face turns red, and he gives Cyllis a flustered shove.

steps.speaker: Ed
steps.content: Oh, cut it out...
Old Rayden loosens the tie he's been adjusting all evening, breathing in the night air as he reflects.

steps.speaker: Rayden
steps.content: It was definitely worth coming. Reminds me of the good old days in the West District...

The group strolls through Eastside's bustling streets, breathing in the night air. Gone are the complaints and frustration they carried when they arrived. Perhaps beautiful music really can cleanse the soul after all.
You catch up to Parfait, eager to ask her the question. Her steps are the lightest of the group, nothing like the composed grace expected of an investment guru.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Hmm? What did you say?
She's still lost in the memory of the performance, completely oblivious to your question.
I mean... you really went through all this trouble to come back just for this concert.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: What else would it be?
Her answer comes so matter-of-factly.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Art exhibitions, concerts, exquisite cuisine... I adore them all. But such pleasures are reserved only for the elite.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: So I schemed my way in—played the fraud, made dirty money, lived in fear of exposure. But I succeeded. And for years, I indulged in every luxury never meant for a West District girl like me.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: But desire is insatiable. And the more I had, the more I wondered. Why? Why are poor people naturally assumed to be incapable of appreciating art and beauty?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Why must humanity's finest creations be gilded cages for the wealthy? I lied, cheated, and bought my way in, so now I'm "worthy." But strip away the silk and jewels, and I'm still that same West District girl.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Which is precisely why I brought my West District friends. Marvels like these—why should wealth dictate who gets to enjoy them? The way they listened tonight... wasn't that proof enough?
You glance back at the group behind you. They're still laughing and chatting animatedly about tonight's concert.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: I've tasted every pleasure and achieved my grandest dream. I suppose my career as a "professional hedonist" hasn't been for nothing... Mm, I have no regrets.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: So now? Let the reckoning come. Punishment, retribution—I'll face it all.

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: I just saw Parfait! She's right over there!
Chaotic footsteps and shouts erupt behind you. Parfait, who just moments ago wore a look of utter defiance, immediately tries to bolt, but her high heels make running impossible.

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: Are you sure the MBCC Chief was among the people who came with Parfait?

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: One hundred percent! I saw them with my own eyes!

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: Wait, they're that close? I heard the Chief turned down Richard's invite. So he basically gave up VIP perks just to sit with Parfait in the regular seats?

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: Doesn't that mean...

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: It means the Chief's actually tight with her. That woman wasn't arrested by MBCC at all, she's just holed up there keeping a low profile!

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: Hey now, watch how you talk. What do you mean by "that woman"? She's the Investment Guru!

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: You have no idea. That Chief's impossible to work with! Every investor in Eastside, from city council members to major developers, has gotten completely shut out. Nobody's getting anywhere near that Syndicate Hypercube mining deal!

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: Wait a minute... What if Parfait's Hypercube mine was actually just a front? Maybe she's been working with West District all along, pulling some kind of bait-and-switch operation.

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: Who knows? But you all saw her tossing Hypercubes from that helicopter like they were candy, right? Let's be real, nobody just "does investments" and gets to shower the streets with Hypercubes.

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: Hold on... Hypercubes, Syndicans, the MBCC Chief... Damn, this is...

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: Stop talking! There she is! Hurry, don't let her get away!

The West District folks with Parfait also hear the commotion behind them and immediately take defensive positions in front of Parfait, their faces grim as if facing a serious threat, but they are quickly overwhelmed by the surging crowd.

steps.speaker: Crowd Voices
steps.content: Where's the Chief? I'm pretty sure I just saw the Chief here too.
Your reaction is much quicker than theirs. Realizing your disguise won't hold up, you have already slipped into a nearby alley before the crowd has a chance to spot you.
Among the crowd, you can faintly make out two somewhat familiar voices.

steps.speaker: Hans
steps.content: Brilliant work, Parfait! She's about to completely flip the game. Though really, if she was holding cards this good, why didn't she tell us sooner?

steps.speaker: Ava
steps.content: Would telling you even help? With that snooty look you give every Syndican, do you really think you could understand Parfait's methods? That's exactly why she's a legend in the investment world.
Parfait is right again. In their line of work, everything comes down to trust and credibility.

When people don't believe in you, no amount of effort can win them over but only scorn. But when they're utterly convinced of something beyond reason, even the most damning scandals become nothing more than charming tales of intrigue.
With these thoughts, you no longer linger in place, striding forward and vanishing into the alley's shadowy depths.

A few days later, on a morning like any other, you arrive at the cafeteria as usual to find Parfait with coffee in one hand and today's financial news in the other—just like when you first met aboard the sand ship.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Good morning, Chief.
I have good news and bad news. Which one do you want to hear first?

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: The bad news, I suppose.
The bad news is, effective immediately, the MBCC cafeteria is no longer available to you.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Good heavens! How could this be?!

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: The MBCC cafeteria's cuisine rivals even Eastside's finest three-star establishments, and yet you would... you would actually bar me from these premises... This is truly the most devastating news I've received all year.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Please, go on and share your good news. I do hope it might soften the blow.
With dramatic flair, Parfait clutches her chest, though she already knows exactly what the good news is.
The good news is right here.
You point to the front page headline of the financial newspaper in her hand.

steps.speaker: Newspapers
steps.content: "Financial Inspection Team Drops Charges Against Parfait; Tulip Holdings Sees Surge in Investor Backing"

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Just this? But this cannot possibly heal the trauma of being banished from the MBCC cafeteria.
Alright, enough with the theatrics. Your company's car is already waiting outside. The long, luxurious one.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: After two whole weeks, it's finally here!

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Won't you come take a look inside? I had the interior custom-designed by the finest artisans. No expense spared, of course. And I always keep my personal wine selection on hand...
Thanks, but I'll pass.
You decline again with a smile. You still remember how she once confidently promised that a car would pick her up, only to end up shivering in the cold for an hour.
Oh, by the way, Cyllis asked me to deliver a message.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Yes?
She said she really liked those high heels you got her, but she ended up breaking them while standing up for you, so she wants you to order her another pair.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Leave it to me!
Parfait sets down her coffee cup and stands up.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Well, it's time to say goodbye. Thank you for having me during this time. Perhaps fate will allow us to meet again...
Wait a moment. There's still something I want to ask you.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: Of course. What is it?
Parfait shows no sign of impatience, looking at you with a warm smile.
The more I've thought about it these past few days, the more something feels wrong... I keep feeling like this whole thing has been off from start to finish.
Why, of all people, did you just happen to get a seat right next to me? Why did your business partner run off exactly the day before you returned, making sure I'd see you at your lowest...?
And why the Spring Concert, where every Eastside elite would be gathered? Why was I recognized despite having a clear disguise...
Then it hit me. You're a professional con artist who built your career on lies. What if... what if this was all an act from the start? Some elaborate scheme to gain my sympathy and help?
Faced with your barrage of questions, Parfait is visibly stunned for a moment.
Then, she flashes you an elegant yet sly smile.

steps.speaker: Parfait
steps.content: So, have you suffered any losses? Will you... expose me?
